quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: More than _________ of motorcycle and car collisions happen because the car driver did not yield to the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car collisions happen because the car driver failed to yield to the motorcycle. Motorcyclists should not assume that car drivers will yield, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always on the left side.
Is always on the right side.

questions.explanation: There is no single lane position that is always safest. Change your position in the lane based on what is happening around you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation best keeps riders close together while maintaining safe space between them?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcycles to stay together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when on a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Not lean with the rider in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. They can also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands before riding.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects against everyday hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop behind it on the roadway.
Stop and wait for it to move.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes to give it more space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle when possible.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car crashes happen at intersections. Usually the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Use it together with the rear brake.
Do not use it — it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles is at intersections.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle stays under control when the rear wheel is locked if the bike is upright and going straight.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when holding the handlebars?
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: How fast does the body remove alcohol?
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies remove about one drink per hour. This rate varies from person to person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Where should you position yourself in your lane to keep other vehicles from sharing it?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to squeeze past you. When you ride behind a car in the center, the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead
Stop completely and go when it is safe

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. When you see one, you must stop completely. Yield to other vehicles and people, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Several surfaces are slippery for motorcycles. These include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates on the road. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal when you finish turning or changing lanes
Use your horn only in emergencies

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal when you finish turning or changing lanes
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you complete a turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers about what you plan to do next.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist NOT do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Choose a position that makes them easier to see
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly
Get ready to use the clutch and brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, stay visible, slow down, and prepare to use your clutch and brakes. Do not speed up. Sudden changes in speed or position can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger do?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when stopped
Sit forward without crowding the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward without crowding the driver
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: If you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: Which item will NOT help protect you from serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also provides protection. A sweatshirt does not offer enough protection.
